series: Why we stop doing things we know are good for us, Reason #18 (the perfect week)
hook: Four workouts a week feels like failing, if you planned seven.

gate.goal_link: any goal with a weekly target (running, gym, a language) dies when good weeks are scored as fails
gate.mechanism: the same output is judged against the plan, not against zero: 4/7 = 57% reads as failure, 4/4 = 100% reads as success, and repeated 'failure' weeks end the habit
gate.universal: almost everyone has planned 7 days and managed 4

frame.obstacle: plans written for a perfect week; real weeks bring meetings, colds, birthdays
frame.cost: 4 runs = 57% of the plan, three 'failed' weeks, then 0
frame.fix: count the last 2 weeks, plan that number, add one after 2 weeks at 100% (the big plan stays as the next level)

hooks_considered.line: Four workouts a week feels like failing, if you planned seven.
hooks_considered.checks: hard truth Y, gap Y, muted Y (57% vs 100% bars), sendable Y, payoff Y

hooks_considered.line: You didn't fail your plan. Your plan assumed a perfect week.
Same four runs. One week is a fail, the other a win.
The day your plan fails isn't Tuesday. It's the day you wrote it.
Most plans are written for a week that never happens.

beats.rehook_10: the real week: misses land on 'meeting', 'cold', 'birthday', 4 of 7
beats.rehook_20: 57% fail, fail, quit -> count the last two weeks
beats.save_moment: PLAN THE REAL WEEK rule card
beats.share_line: Send this to the friend who plans seven and quits in week two.
beats.comment_q: How many days did you really manage last week?

note: Pillar A. Big plan is not the villain: it returns as 'add one after two weeks at 100%'. gym-calendar gained stage 'real' (misses with reasons, counter counts ticks only); input-week gained `unit`.
